basis: Peripheral nerve proliferations characteristically occupy oral mucosa, especially lips and tongue; associated MEN2B endocrine tumours are separate.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: characteristic neuromas arise in oral mucosa, including the tongue and lips.

basis: Complex II deficiency is a metabolic disorder; the supplied definition identifies neurological and muscular manifestations as its defining organ phenotype.

decisions.neurologic: primary: neurological manifestations are explicitly part of the supplied disease definition.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: muscular manifestations are explicitly part of the supplied mitochondrial disease definition.

basis: Limb malformations, ectodermal dysplasia and oral clefting define EEC1. Damaging ocular involvement at >=30% is not established for this subtype.

decisions.ocular: none: ocular findings have unspecified frequencies; common lacrimal disease in other EEC forms cannot establish >=30% involvement in EEC1.

basis: Ataxia and polyneuropathy define neurologic disease; supplied ancestry explicitly classifies the underlying disorder among inborn errors of metabolism.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: the supplied ancestry explicitly identifies an inborn metabolic disorder, supporting the metabolic mechanism axis.

basis: Neurologic degeneration and cutaneous photosensitivity characterize disease; sensorineural hearing loss occurs in 30-79%. Calcification alone does not establish vascular dysfunction.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: premature atherosclerosis (30-79%) is a separate disease; vascular calcification alone does not demonstrate functional vascular damage.

basis: Chronic airway disease spanning neutrophilic and paucigranulocytic endotypes; an immune-mediated mechanism is not established across most of this umbrella.

decisions.infectious_immune: none: this umbrella includes paucigranulocytic disease with nonimmune mechanisms; neutrophilic inflammation does not establish immune mediation across most cases.

basis: PXE is an elastic-tissue disorder of skin, ocular tissues and arterial walls, with attenuated expression here. Gastrointestinal and cerebral hemorrhage are minority complications.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: arterial elastic-tissue disease is a defining location of PXE; the record supports arterial mineralization and occlusive stenosis.

basis: Complement-mediated hemolysis, thrombocytopenia and renal injury define aHUS; direct microvascular endothelial injury and thrombosis are intrinsic in essentially all cases.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: defining thrombotic microangiopathy directly injures capillaries in essentially all cases; cardiovascular includes microvessels, not just the heart.

basis: Mitochondrial disease with defining optic atrophy; neuropathy, ataxia or developmental impairment affect most patients; auditory neuropathy/hearing loss occurs in roughly 40-50%.

decisions.otologic: involved: auditory neuropathy or hearing loss affects roughly 40-50% across reported FDXR disease cohorts, exceeding the threshold.

basis: ALP deficiency causes severe skeletal hypomineralization; defective dental mineralization and premature tooth loss commonly affect surviving children (>30%).

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: intrinsic dental mineralization and cementum defects with premature tooth loss commonly affect infantile HPP during childhood (>30%).
